caption: 01 · PREPARE — Who should speak and under what conditions?. Define purpose, interviewer, narrator, consent, accessibility, language, compensation, privacy, cultural authority, distress protocol, topics declined, recording ownership, and withdrawal limits.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping who should speak and under what conditions? within The Oral History Is a Succession Document.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · ELICIT — Which decisions cannot be read from files?. Ask for sensory thresholds, rejected options, relationship dynamics, exceptions, informal vocabulary, moments of uncertainty, and what the narrator does not know.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping which decisions cannot be read from files? within The Oral History Is a Succession Document.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · CORRECT — Can narrators revise the record?. Provide transcript, contextual notes, name and pronoun checks, redaction, embargo, restriction, disagreement, and approval choices without promising control the archive cannot legally grant.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can narrators revise the record? within The Oral History Is a Succession Document.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

caption: 04 · CONNECT — How does voice join the archive?. Bind recording, transcript, timecodes, people, objects, files, rights, access, preservation copies, migrations, and successor-use rules through stable identifiers.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
